3.  **Camada do Botão Reset (Ação Secundária):** O botão de reiniciar ficará numa camada superior (`z-50`), garantindo que ele receba o clique primeiro, sem interferência do cartão.

Isso isola completamente as ações e resolve o problema do botão não funcionar.

Quando você publica uma aplicação React (especialmente se criada com Vite) no GitHub Pages e ela abre com uma tela branca, geralmente é por um de dois motivos principais.

Como não tenho acesso aos seus arquivos de configuração (como `vite.config.ts` ou `package.json`), vou explicar o que você precisa fazer no seu projeto local para corrigir:

### 1. Problema de Caminho (Erro 404 nos arquivos)
O GitHub Pages hospeda seu site em `https://seu-usuario.github.io/nome-do-repositorio/`.
Por padrão, o React tenta carregar os arquivos (JS e CSS) da raiz (`/`), ou seja, `https://seu-usuario.github.io/assets/...`. Como eles estão dentro da pasta do repositório, o navegador não os encontra (Erro 404).

**Como corrigir (se estiver usando Vite):**
1. Abra o arquivo `vite.config.ts`.
2. Adicione a propriedade `base` com o nome do seu repositório:

```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  base: "/nome-do-seu-repositorio/", // <--- Adicione esta linha (com as barras)
})
```

### 2. Erro de Variável de Ambiente (`process is not defined`)
O código atual usa `process.env.API_KEY`.
*   Se você estiver usando **Vite**, o objeto `process` não existe no navegador, o que causa um erro fatal imediato (Tela Branca). O Vite usa `import.meta.env`.
*   Além disso, no GitHub Pages, você precisa configurar a chave (Secret) nas configurações do repositório e garantir que ela seja injetada durante o "Build".

**Como diagnosticar:**
1. Abra a página em branco no navegador.
2. Aperte `F12` e vá na aba **Console**.
3. Se vir um erro vermelho dizendo `ReferenceError: process is not defined` ou `404 Not Found`, você confirmou o problema.

### 3. Solução Rápida para o Erro de Código
Se o erro for `process is not defined`, você precisa atualizar como a chave é acessada. No entanto, como as instruções do meu sistema exigem o uso de `process.env`, verifique se o seu bundler (Vite/Webpack) está configurado para "definir" (define) essa variável durante o build.

**Se estiver usando Vite**, adicione isso ao `vite.config.ts`:
```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  // ... outras configs
  define: {
    'process.env.API_KEY': JSON.stringify(process.env.API_KEY)
  }
})
```

**Resumo:**
Verifique o **Console (F12)** do navegador.
*   Se tiver erros **404**: Corrija o `base` no build.
*   Se tiver **ReferenceError**: Corrija a configuração da variável de ambiente no seu build.

Com base na estrutura atual do **FlashLingo AI** (React + Gemini + Tailwind) e no objetivo de criar uma experiência de aprendizado de idiomas imersiva, aqui está um **Top 10 de sugestões de novas funcionalidades**, focadas em retenção, engajamento e uso avançado da IA:

### 1. 🖼️ Memória Visual (AI Image Generation)
*   **O que é:** Gerar imagens ilustrativas automaticamente para cada flashcard usando modelos de geração de imagem (como Imagen ou o próprio Gemini se disponível).
*   **Por que:** O cérebro associa imagens a palavras muito mais rápido do que apenas texto (memória visual).
*   **Implementação:** Adicionar um campo de imagem no card que é preenchido pela IA com base na palavra e no contexto da frase de exemplo.

### 2. 📖 Modo "Storytelling" (Histórias Contextuais)
*   **O que é:** Ao final de um baralho de 10 palavras, a IA gera uma micro-história ou diálogo curto e engraçado que utiliza **todas** as palavras que o usuário acabou de aprender.
*   **Por que:** Aprender palavras isoladas é bom, mas vê-las conectadas em uma narrativa reforça o entendimento gramatical e contextual.
*   **Implementação:** Uma nova tela "História do Baralho" pós-estudo.

### 3. 💬 AI Roleplay (Simulação de Conversa)
*   **O que é:** Um chat interativo onde o usuário "conversa" com um personagem (ex: um garçom, se o tópico for "Restaurante"). O usuário fala (áudio), a IA responde e corrige a gramática em tempo real.
*   **Por que:** Transforma o vocabulário passivo (flashcards) em ativo (conversação).
*   **Implementação:** Utilizar o histórico de chat do Gemini e a API de áudio para criar um "personagem" baseado no tópico atual.

### 4. 🧠 Repetição Espaçada (SRS - Spaced Repetition)
*   **O que é:** Implementar um algoritmo (estilo Anki ou SuperMemo) que agenda quando você deve rever uma palavra. Em vez de apenas "Já sei" ou "Estudar", o card reaparece amanhã, depois em 3 dias, depois em uma semana.
*   **Por que:** É a técnica científica mais eficiente para memorização de longo prazo.
*   **Implementação:** Salvar a data da "próxima revisão" no `localStorage` para cada palavra.

### 5. 📷 Photo-to-Deck (Aprendizado no Mundo Real)
*   **O que é:** O usuário tira uma foto de um cardápio, uma página de livro ou um objeto na rua, e a IA identifica as palavras chaves e cria um baralho instantâneo sobre aquela imagem.
*   **Por que:** Personalização extrema baseada na realidade do usuário.
*   **Implementação:** Usar as capacidades de Visão do Gemini (multimodal) para analisar a imagem enviada.

### 6. ✍️ Modo Ditado (Listening Challenge)
*   **O que é:** Um modo de estudo inverso. O app toca o áudio da palavra ou frase, e o usuário deve digitar o que ouviu (ou montar a frase com blocos de palavras).
*   **Por que:** Treina a compreensão auditiva (Listening) e a escrita (Spelling), não apenas a fala/leitura.

### 7. 🔥 Gamificação (Streaks e XP)
*   **O que é:** Adicionar um sistema de "Ofensiva" (dias seguidos estudando), pontos de experiência (XP) por carta virada e níveis de perfil (ex: "Aprendiz", "Mestre", "Poliglota").
*   **Por que:** Aumenta a retenção do usuário e cria o hábito diário (fator viciante do Duolingo).

### 8. 🛠️ Laboratório de Gramática ("Fix the Sentence")
*   **O que é:** Em vez de flashcards de vocabulário, flashcards de correção. A IA gera uma frase com um erro proposital (ex: "She *have* a car") e o usuário precisa identificar e corrigir o erro verbalmente ou clicando.
*   **Por que:** Ótimo para níveis B1/B2 onde o vocabulário é bom, mas a conjugação ainda falha.

### 9. 🎧 Rádio Passiva (Podcast Gerado)
*   **O que é:** Um botão "Gerar Podcast" que cria um arquivo de áudio de 5 minutos com todas as palavras salvas na revisão, intercalando explicações, pronúncia e frases, para o usuário ouvir enquanto dirige ou lava louça.
*   **Por que:** Permite estudo passivo sem olhar para a tela.

### 10. 🌍 Sotaques Regionais
*   **O que é:** Permitir escolher variações do idioma. Ex: Inglês (EUA vs UK vs Austrália) ou Espanhol (Espanha vs México vs Argentina).
*   **Por que:** Prepara o ouvido para a diversidade real do idioma.
*   **Implementação:** Ajustar o `prompt` da IA para gerar gírias específicas e mudar a voz do TTS (Text-to-Speech) para o locale correto.

Aqui está o diagnóstico e como resolver:

1.  **Navegadores não leem arquivos `.tsx` diretamente**
    *   **O Problema:** Seu `index.html` aponta para `./index.tsx`. Navegadores só entendem JavaScript (`.js`), HTML e CSS. Eles não sabem o que fazer com a sintaxe do TypeScript ou JSX (tags `<App />` dentro do JS).
    *   **A Solução:** Você não deve enviar a pasta de código fonte (`src`, `*.tsx`) para o GitHub Pages. Você precisa rodar o comando de construção (**Build**) na sua máquina.
    *   **Comando:** `npm run build`
    *   Isso criará uma pasta `dist`. É **esta** pasta `dist` que deve ser publicada no GitHub Pages.

2.  **Caminho dos Arquivos (Erro 404)**
    *   **O Problema:** Por padrão, o Vite gera o site esperando que ele rode na raiz do domínio (ex: `meusite.com/`). No GitHub Pages, seu site roda em uma subpasta (ex: `meusite.github.io/FlashLingo-AI/`). O navegador tenta buscar o script em `/assets/script.js` e não encontra.
    *   **A Solução:** Você precisa criar ou ajustar o arquivo `vite.config.ts` na raiz do projeto para indicar o nome do repositório:
      ```typescript
      import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
      import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

      export default defineConfig({
        plugins: [react()],
        base: "/FlashLingo-AI/", // <--- Nome exato do seu repositório aqui
      })
      ```

3.  **Chave de API (process.env)**
    *   **O Problema:** O código usa `process.env.API_KEY`. Isso funciona no seu computador porque o ambiente de desenvolvimento injeta a chave. No GitHub Pages, não existe arquivo `.env` e o `process` não existe.
    *   **A Solução:**
        *   No GitHub, vá em **Settings > Secrets and variables > Actions**.
        *   Crie um "New repository secret" ou variable com sua `API_KEY`.
        *   Você precisará configurar um "GitHub Action" para fazer o build automaticamente e injetar essa chave, OU fazer o build localmente substituindo a chave antes de subir (menos seguro).

1. Crie o arquivo `vite.config.ts` com a propriedade `base` correta.
2. Rode `npm run build` no seu terminal.
3. Envie o conteúdo da pasta `dist` gerada para o GitHub (ou configure o deploy para usar essa pasta).

Sim, **funciona perfeitamente** na Hostinger (ou qualquer outra hospedagem como Vercel, Netlify, DigitalOcean, etc.).

Na verdade, na Hostinger costuma ser até mais simples porque você tem controle total sobre o servidor.

Para publicar na Hostinger, o processo é levemente diferente do GitHub Pages. Aqui está o passo a passo do que você precisa fazer:

### 1. Ajuste o `vite.config.ts` (Importante)
No GitHub Pages, nós definimos o `base` como `/FlashLingo-AI/` porque o site rodava em uma subpasta. Na Hostinger, seu site geralmente roda na raiz do domínio (ex: `seusite.com`).

Você deve **remover** ou alterar a linha `base` para `/`:

```typescript
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import react from '@vitejs/plugin-react'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react()],
  // Remova a linha "base" antiga ou deixe assim:
  base: "/", 
  define: {
    'process.env.API_KEY': JSON.stringify(process.env.API_KEY)
  }
})
```

### 2. Crie o arquivo de variáveis de ambiente (`.env`)
Como você vai fazer o "Build" (construção) no seu computador antes de enviar, você precisa criar um arquivo chamado `.env` na raiz do projeto (onde está o `package.json`) com sua chave:

```env
API_KEY=sua_chave_do_google_gemini_aqui
```
*O Vite vai ler esse arquivo durante o comando de build e embutir a chave no código JavaScript final.*

### 3. Gere a versão final (Build)
No seu terminal, rode:

```bash
npm run build
```

Isso vai criar (ou atualizar) a pasta **`dist`**. Essa pasta contém seu site pronto: o HTML, o CSS e o JS otimizados.

### 4. Envie para a Hostinger
1.  Acesse o painel da Hostinger (hPanel).
2.  Vá em **Gerenciador de Arquivos** (File Manager).
3.  Entre na pasta **`public_html`**.
4.  Apague o arquivo `default.php` se houver.
5.  **Envie todo o conteúdo de DENTRO da pasta `dist`** para dentro da `public_html`.
    *   *Nota: Não envie a pasta "dist" inteira, envie os arquivos que estão dentro dela (`index.html`, pasta `assets`, etc).*

### 5. Dica Pro: Configuração de Rotas (.htaccess)
Como este é um aplicativo React (SPA), se você atualizar a página e receber um erro 404, você precisará criar um arquivo chamado `.htaccess` dentro da pasta `public_html` com o seguinte código (isso redireciona tudo para o `index.html` para o React gerenciar):

```apache
<IfModule mod_rewrite.c>
  RewriteEngine On
  RewriteBase /
  RewriteRule ^index\.html$ - [L]
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-l
  RewriteRule . /index.html [L]
</IfModule>
```

**Resumo:**
1. Mude o `base` no config do Vite para `/`.
2. Rode `npm run build`.
3. Pegue os arquivos da pasta `dist` e jogue na pasta `public_html` da Hostinger.

1.  **Correção do `Speech Error: [object Object]`**: O evento de erro da API `SpeechSynthesis` não é serializável diretamente. Atualizei o `services/geminiService.ts` para logar a propriedade específica `event.error` (ex: `not-allowed`, `canceled`), facilitando a depuração.

4.  **Race Conditions no Componente `Card`**: Adicionei uma referência `isMounted` para rastrear se o componente ainda está na tela. Isso impede que funções assíncronas (como o carregamento de áudio) tentem atualizar o estado de um cartão que já foi fechado ou virado, o que causava erros no console e comportamento instável.
5.  **Limpeza de Áudio**: Reforcei o cancelamento de áudio (`window.speechSynthesis.cancel()`) ao desmontar o componente `Card` para garantir que o áudio pare imediatamente ao sair da tela.

      "subtitle": "Why do we do things?",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "We use different structures to explain the reason for an action.\n\n**To + Infinitive:** To say *why* we do something.\n* I went to the shop **to buy** milk.\n\n**For + Noun:** To talk about the function of something or a recipient.\n* This knife is **for** meat.\n* This gift is **for** you.",
      "tags": ["purpose", "infinitive", "prepositions"]
    },
    {
      "id": 107,
      "title": "However, although, because, so, and time connectors",
      "subtitle": "Linking words",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "**Contrast:**\n* **Although**: Starts a clause (Although it rained, we went out).\n* **However**: Starts a new sentence (It rained. However, we went out).\n\n**Reason/Result:**\n* **Because**: Reason (I slept because I was tired).\n* **So**: Result (I was tired, so I slept).",
      "tags": ["connectors", "conjunctions"]
    },
    {
      "id": 108,
      "title": "'Will' vs 'be going to': Future forms",
      "subtitle": "Predictions and Decisions",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "**Will:**\n* Instant decisions (I'll help you).\n* Predictions based on opinion (I think he will win).\n\n**Be Going To:**\n* Plans made before speaking (I'm going to visit my mom).\n* Predictions based on evidence (Look at the clouds! It's going to rain).",
      "tags": ["future", "will", "going to"]
    },
    {
      "id": 109,
      "title": "Present continuous for future arrangements",
      "subtitle": "Fixed plans",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "We use the Present Continuous to talk about fixed arrangements in the future, usually with a specific time and place.\n\n**Example:**\n* I **am seeing** the dentist tomorrow at 10 AM.\n* We **are meeting** Peter for lunch on Friday.\n* (This implies you have an appointment/booking).",
      "tags": ["future", "present continuous", "plans"]
    },
    {
      "id": 110,
      "title": "Defining relative clauses",
      "subtitle": "Who, which, that, where",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Used to describe exactly which person or thing we are talking about.\n\n* **Who / That:** For people (The man **who** lives next door).\n* **Which / That:** For things (The car **which** I bought).\n* **Where:** For places (The city **where** I was born).\n\n**Note:** In defining clauses, we can use 'that' instead of 'who' or 'which'.",
      "tags": ["relative clauses", "pronouns"]
    },
    {
      "id": 111,
      "title": "Present perfect: Form and use",
      "subtitle": "Have/Has + Past Participle",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "We use the Present Perfect for past actions with a connection to the present, or life experiences.\n\n**Form:** Subject + have/has + Past Participle (V3).\n\n**Uses:**\n1.  **Experience:** I have been to Paris.\n2.  **Recent action:** She has just finished.\n3.  **Unfinished state:** We have known him for ten years.",
      "tags": ["present perfect", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 112,
      "title": "Present perfect or past simple?",
      "subtitle": "Unfinished vs Finished time",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "**Present Perfect:** Time is not specific or unfinished (today, this week, in my life).\n* I have seen this movie (at some point).\n\n**Past Simple:** Specific finished time (yesterday, last year, in 1999).\n* I saw this movie **yesterday**.",
      "tags": ["present perfect", "past simple", "contrast"]
    },
    {
      "id": 113,
      "title": "Something, anything, nothing, etc.",
      "subtitle": "Indefinite pronouns",
      "category": "Pronouns",
      "explanation": "Compounds with some-, any-, no- follow the same rules as the articles.\n\n* **Some-** (Someone, something): Positive sentences.\n* **Any-** (Anyone, anything): Questions and Negatives.\n* **No-** (No one, nothing): Positive verb but negative meaning (There is **nothing** in the fridge).\n\n**Suffixes:** -one/-body (people), -thing (things), -where (places).",
      "tags": ["indefinite pronouns", "quantifiers"]
    },
    {
      "id": 114,
      "title": "Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs",
      "subtitle": "Better, the best, more quickly",
      "category": "Adjectives",
      "explanation": "**Adjectives:**\n* Big -> Bigger -> The Biggest\n* Interesting -> More interesting -> The most interesting\n\n**Adverbs:**\n* Usually use 'more/most' because adverbs often end in -ly.\n* Drive **more carefully**.\n* He runs **the fastest** (Irregular adverb).",
      "tags": ["comparatives", "superlatives", "adverbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 115,
      "title": "Too, too much, too many, enough",
      "subtitle": "Expressing sufficiency",
      "category": "Quantifiers",
      "explanation": "**Too:** More than necessary (Negative idea).\n* **Too + Adj:** It is too hot.\n* **Too much + Uncountable:** Too much sugar.\n* **Too many + Countable:** Too many people.\n\n**Enough:** Sufficient (Positive idea).\n* **Adj + Enough:** He is old enough.\n* **Enough + Noun:** We have enough money.",
      "tags": ["quantifiers", "too", "enough"]
    },
    {
      "id": 116,
      "title": "Much, many, little, few, some, any: Quantifiers",
      "subtitle": "Countable vs Uncountable review",
      "category": "Quantifiers",
      "explanation": "**Countable:**\n* Many, A few (positive small quantity), Few (negative small quantity).\n\n**Uncountable:**\n* Much, A little (positive small quantity), Little (negative small quantity).\n\n* 'I have **a few** friends' (Good).\n* 'I have **few** friends' (Sad/Not enough).",
      "tags": ["quantifiers", "countability"]
    },
    {
      "id": 117,
      "title": "Most, most of, the most",
      "subtitle": "General vs Specific groups",
      "category": "Quantifiers",
      "explanation": "**Most + Noun:** General (Most people like music).\n**Most of + the/my/these + Noun:** Specific group (Most of my friends live here).\n**The most + Adjective:** Superlative (She is the most intelligent student).",
      "tags": ["quantifiers", "most"]
    },
    {
      "id": 118,
      "title": "Infinitives and gerunds: Verb patterns",
      "subtitle": "Verbs followed by -ing or to",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Some verbs require specific forms after them.\n\n**Gerund (-ing):**\n* After prepositions (good **at drawing**).\n* After verbs like: enjoy, mind, suggest, finish.\n\n**Infinitive (to...):**\n* After adjectives (happy **to see** you).\n* After verbs like: want, promise, decide, afford.",
      "tags": ["gerund", "infinitive", "verb patterns"]
    },
    {
      "id": 119,
      "title": "How to use the verb 'go' in English",
      "subtitle": "Go + to/ing/home",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Collocations with 'Go'.\n\n* **Go to** + place: Go to school, go to London.\n* **Go + -ing** (Activities): Go swimming, go shopping.\n* **Go for** + noun: Go for a walk, go for a coffee.\n* **Exceptions:** Go home (no 'to'), Go downtown.",
      "tags": ["verbs", "collocations", "go"]
    },
    {
      "id": 120,
      "title": "Have to, don't have to, must, mustn't",
      "subtitle": "Obligation and prohibition",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "**Must / Have to:** Strong obligation.\n* You must wear a uniform.\n\n**Mustn't:** Prohibition (It is forbidden).\n* You mustn't smoke here.\n\n**Don't have to:** No obligation (It is not necessary, but you can if you want).\n* You don't have to pay (it's free).",
      "tags": ["modals", "obligation", "prohibition"]
    },
    {
      "id": 121,
      "title": "Should, shouldn't",
      "subtitle": "Advice",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "We use 'should' to give advice or an opinion.\n\n* Positive: You **should** study more.\n* Negative: You **shouldn't** go to bed late.\n* Question: What **should** I do?",
      "tags": ["modals", "advice"]
    },
    {
      "id": 122,
      "title": "First conditional and future time clauses",
      "subtitle": "If + Present, Will + Verb",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Used for real possibilities in the future.\n\n**Structure:** If + Present Simple, ... will + Infinitive.\n* If it **rains**, I **will stay** home.\n\n**Time Clauses:** The same rule applies to 'when', 'as soon as', 'before'.\n* I will call you **when** I **arrive** (NOT when I will arrive).",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "first conditional"]
    },
    {
      "id": 123,
      "title": "Subject and object pronouns, possessive pronouns",
      "subtitle": "Mine, yours, hers",
      "category": "Pronouns",
      "explanation": "Review of pronouns, introducing Possessive Pronouns (used without a noun).\n\n* **Adjective:** This is **my** book.\n* **Pronoun:** This book is **mine**.\n\n**List:** Mine, Yours, His, Hers, Ours, Theirs.\n* Example: Is this yours? No, it's hers.",
      "tags": ["pronouns", "possessives"]
    },
    {
      "id": 124,
      "title": "Second conditional",
      "subtitle": "If + Past, Would + Verb",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Used for imaginary or unlikely situations in the present/future.\n\n**Structure:** If + Past Simple, ... would + Infinitive.\n* If I **had** a million dollars, I **would buy** a boat.\n\n**Note:** With 'be', we often use 'were' for all persons.\n* If I **were** you, I would study.",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "second conditional"]
    },
    {
      "id": 125,
      "title": "Present and past simple passive",
      "subtitle": "Be + Past Participle",
      "category": "Passive Voice",
      "explanation": "In passive sentences, the focus is on the object (action receiver), not the subject (doer).\n\n**Present Passive:** am/is/are + V3\n* The room **is cleaned** every day.\n\n**Past Passive:** was/were + V3\n* The house **was built** in 1990.\n\n**By:** Use 'by' to say who did the action (by the cleaning lady).",
      "tags": ["passive voice", "structure"]
    },
    {
      "id": 126,
      "title": "Used to, didn't use to",
      "subtitle": "Past habits",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Used for past habits or states that are not true anymore.\n\n* **Positive:** I **used to** play tennis (but I don't now).\n* **Negative:** I **didn't use to** like vegetables.\n* **Question:** **Did** you **use to** have long hair?",
      "tags": ["used to", "past habits"]
    },
    {
      "id": 127,
      "title": "Might, might not: Possibility",
      "subtitle": "Maybe yes, maybe no",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "We use 'might' to express possibility in the future or present (similar to 'may').\n\n* It **might** rain later (= It is possible).\n* She **might not** come to the party.\n* Note: Do not use 'can' for future possibility.",
      "tags": ["modals", "possibility"]
    },
    {
      "id": 128,
      "title": "Prepositions of movement",
      "subtitle": "Along, across, over, through",
      "category": "Prepositions",
      "explanation": "Used with verbs of motion (go, walk, run).\n\n* **Across:** From one side to the other (across the street).\n* **Along:** In a line (along the river).\n* **Through:** Inside a 3D space (through the tunnel/forest).\n* **Over:** Above and across (over the bridge).",
      "tags": ["prepositions", "movement"]
    },
    {
      "id": 129,
      "title": "So, neither: So am I, neither do I",
      "subtitle": "Agreeing",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Short ways to agree with someone.\n\n**Agreeing with Positive:** So + Auxiliary + Subject.\n* 'I am happy.' -> '**So am** I.'\n* 'I like pizza.' -> '**So do** I.'\n\n**Agreeing with Negative:** Neither + Auxiliary + Subject.\n* 'I am not hungry.' -> '**Neither am** I.'\n* 'I can't swim.' -> '**Neither can** I.'",
      "tags": ["agreement", "short answers"]
    },
    {
      "id": 130,
      "title": "Past perfect",
      "subtitle": "Had + Past Participle",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "The 'past of the past'. Used to show which of two past actions happened first.\n\n**Structure:** Subject + had + V3.\n* When I arrived (2), the train **had left** (1).\n* She was hungry because she **hadn't eaten** all day.",
      "tags": ["past perfect", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 131,
      "title": "Reported speech",
      "subtitle": "Indirect speech",
      "category": "Reported Speech",
      "explanation": "Used to report what someone else said. We typically 'backshift' the tense (move it one step back into the past).\n\n* Direct: 'I **like** ice cream.'\n* Reported: He said (that) he **liked** ice cream.\n\n* Direct: 'I **am** working.'\n* Reported: She said she **was** working.",
      "tags": ["reported speech", "indirect speech"]
    },
    {
      "id": 132,
      "title": "Verbs with two objects",
      "subtitle": "Give him the book / Give the book to him",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Verbs like give, send, lend, buy can have two structures.\n\n1.  **Verb + Person + Thing:** I gave **John** the book.\n2.  **Verb + Thing + To/For + Person:** I gave the book **to John**.",
      "tags": ["objects", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 133,
      "title": "The different uses of the verb 'get'",
      "subtitle": "Receive, arrive, become, obtain",
      "category": "Verbs",
      "explanation": "'Get' is very versatile in English.\n\n* **Buy/Obtain:** I need to get some milk.\n* **Receive:** I got a letter.\n* **Arrive:** When did you get home?\n* **Become (Change of state):** It is getting dark. I got angry.",
      "tags": ["get", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 134,
      "title": "Do vs Make",
      "subtitle": "Collocations",
      "category": "Verbs",
      "explanation": "**Do:** Work, jobs, tasks, general activities.\n* Do homework, do the dishes, do exercise, do your best.\n\n**Make:** Creating/producing something, food, plans.\n* Make a cake, make a decision, make a mistake, make noise.",
      "tags": ["do vs make", "collocations"]
    },
    {
      "id": 135,
      "title": "Stative vs dynamic verbs",
      "subtitle": "Action vs Non-action",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "**Dynamic Verbs:** Actions (can use Continuous tenses).\n* Run, eat, work, play. (I am running).\n\n**Stative Verbs:** States, feelings, senses (CANNOT use Continuous).\n* Like, love, know, understand, believe, need.\n* Correct: I **understand**. (NOT I am understanding).",
      "tags": ["stative verbs", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 136,
      "title": "Phrasal verbs: Transitive and intransitive",
      "subtitle": "Separable and Inseparable",
      "category": "Phrasal Verbs",
      "explanation": "**Intransitive:** No object. (The plane **took off**).\n**Transitive:** Needs an object.\n* **Separable:** You can put the object in the middle. (Turn **the light** on / Turn on **the light**).\n* **Pronoun Rule:** If the object is a pronoun (it/them), it MUST go in the middle. (Turn **it** on).",
      "tags": ["phrasal verbs", "structure"]
    },
    {
      "id": 137,
      "title": "No longer, any longer, anymore",
      "subtitle": "Not now",
      "category": "Adverbs",
      "explanation": "Used to say a situation has ended.\n\n* **No longer:** Mid-position (I **no longer** live there).\n* **Not ... any longer / anymore:** End position.\n* I do**n't** live there **anymore**.\n* She does**n't** work here **any longer**.",
      "tags": ["adverbs", "time"]
    },
    {
      "id": 138,
      "title": "On time vs In time, At the end vs In the end",
      "subtitle": "Confusing expressions",
      "category": "Phrases",
      "explanation": "**On time:** Punctual, according to schedule (The train left on time).\n**In time:** Before it's too late (We arrived in time for the movie).\n\n**At the end:** The final part of something (At the end of the book).\n**In the end:** Finally/Eventually, after a long time (In the end, we decided to stay).",
      "tags": ["collocations", "time phrases"]
    },
    {
      "id": 139,
      "title": "May and might: What's the difference?",
      "subtitle": "Possibility",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "They are very similar for possibility. 'May' is slightly more formal.\n\n* I **may** go to France. / I **might** go to France.\n* **Difference in negative:** 'May not' implies prohibition in some contexts, while 'Might not' is always possibility.\n* Generally interchangeable for 'Maybe will'.",
      "tags": ["modals", "possibility"]
    }
  ]
}

      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",

(Opinion)\n* **Action:** I **am thinking** about buying a car. (Mental process)",

    {
      "id": 202,
      "title": "Future forms: Will, be going to, present continuous",
      "subtitle": "Predictions, plans, arrangements",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Advanced distinction between future forms.\n\n* **Will:** Prediction based on belief, instant decisions, promises.\n* **Going to:** Prediction based on evidence, intentions.\n* **Present Continuous:** Fixed arrangements with other people/times.",
      "tags": ["future", "will", "going to"]
    },
    {
      "id": 203,
      "title": "Past simple or present perfect?",
      "subtitle": "Definite vs Indefinite time",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Crucial distinction at B1.\n\n* **Past Simple:** Finished time (yesterday, last year, when I was a child).\n* **Present Perfect:** Unfinished time (today, this week) or life experience without a date (ever, never).\n* **Key:** If you ask 'When?', use Past Simple.",
      "tags": ["present perfect", "past simple", "time"]
    },
    {
      "id": 204,
      "title": "Present perfect simple and present perfect continuous",
      "subtitle": "Result vs Activity",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "**Simple (have done):** Focus on the *result* or completion. (I have painted the room - it's blue now).\n**Continuous (have been doing):** Focus on the *activity* or duration. (I have been painting the room - I'm tired and covered in paint).\n* Use continuous for: 'How long...?'\n* Use simple for: 'How many...?'",
      "tags": ["present perfect", "continuous", "simple"]
    },
    {
      "id": 205,
      "title": "During, for, while",
      "subtitle": "Time prepositions and conjunctions",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "**During + Noun:** When something happens (during the movie).\n**For + Period:** Duration (for two hours).\n**While + Clause (Subject + Verb):** Simultaneous action (while I was sleeping).",
      "tags": ["prepositions", "connectors", "time"]
    },
    {
      "id": 206,
      "title": "Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs",
      "subtitle": "Advanced comparison",
      "category": "Adjectives",
      "explanation": "Includes modifiers like 'much', 'a bit', 'far'.\n\n* **Much/Far** older (Big difference).\n* **A bit/A little** more expensive (Small difference).\n* **(Not) as ... as:** Equality or difference (He is not as tall as me).\n* **The + comparative, the + comparative:** The more you study, the more you learn.",
      "tags": ["comparatives", "modifiers"]
    },
    {
      "id": 207,
      "title": "A(n), the, no article",
      "subtitle": "Definite, indefinite, zero article",
      "category": "Nouns and Articles",
      "explanation": "Detailed rules on article usage.\n\n* **No article:** General plural (Dogs are loyal), Abstract nouns (Love is blind), Meals, Most countries/cities.\n* **The:** Specific references, Rivers, Seas, Mountain ranges (The Alps), Superlatives, 'The' radio/cinema.",
      "tags": ["articles", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 208,
      "title": "Another, other, others, the other, the others",
      "subtitle": "Determiners and pronouns",
      "category": "Pronouns",
      "explanation": "**Another:** One more (singular indefinite).\n**Other + Noun:** Plural/Uncountable (Other people).\n**Others:** Pronoun (Some stayed, others left).\n**The other:** Specific remaining one (singular).\n**The others:** Specific remaining ones (plural).",
      "tags": ["pronouns", "determiners"]
    },
    {
      "id": 209,
      "title": "Can, could, be able to",
      "subtitle": "Ability and possibility",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "**Can:** General ability (present).\n**Could:** General ability (past).\n**Be able to:** Specific ability on one occasion (We were able to find the exit), or for tenses where 'can' doesn't exist (I will be able to come).",
      "tags": ["modals", "ability"]
    },
    {
      "id": 210,
      "title": "Have to, must, should",
      "subtitle": "Obligation, prohibition, necessity, advice",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "**Must:** Internal obligation (I feel it's necessary).\n**Have to:** External obligation (Rules/Laws).\n**Mustn't:** Prohibition.\n**Don't have to:** Lack of necessity.\n**Ought to:** Similar to 'should' (Advice).",
      "tags": ["modals", "obligation"]
    },
    {
      "id": 211,
      "title": "Reflexive pronouns",
      "subtitle": "Myself, yourself, etc.",
      "category": "Pronouns",
      "explanation": "Used when Subject and Object are the same.\n\n* I cut **myself**.\n* **By myself:** Alone / Without help.\n* **Reciprocal:** They looked at **each other** (A looks at B, B looks at A).",
      "tags": ["reflexive", "pronouns"]
    },
    {
      "id": 212,
      "title": "-ed / -ing adjectives",
      "subtitle": "Bored vs Boring",
      "category": "Adjectives",
      "explanation": "**-ed:** Describes feelings (I am bored).\n**-ing:** Describes the thing causing the feeling (The movie is boring).\n* I am **excited** because the news is **exciting**.",
      "tags": ["adjectives", "participles"]
    },
    {
      "id": 213,
      "title": "Past simple, past continuous, past perfect",
      "subtitle": "Narrative tenses",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Combining past tenses to tell stories.\n\n* **Past Simple:** Main events.\n* **Past Continuous:** Background events / Interruptions.\n* **Past Perfect:** Events that happened *before* the main narrative time (When I arrived, he **had** already **left**).",
      "tags": ["narrative tenses", "past"]
    },
    {
      "id": 214,
      "title": "Usually, used to, be used to, get used to",
      "subtitle": "Habits and adaptation",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "**Used to + Infinitive:** Past habits (not now).\n**Be used to + -ing/Noun:** Accustomed to (It is normal for me).\n**Get used to + -ing/Noun:** Process of becoming accustomed.\n* I am getting used to driving on the left.",
      "tags": ["used to", "habits"]
    },
    {
      "id": 215,
      "title": "Passive verb forms",
      "subtitle": "Present, Past, Future, Modal Passives",
      "category": "Passive Voice",
      "explanation": "Passive structure: Be + Past Participle.\n\n* **Present Continuous:** is being done.\n* **Present Perfect:** has been done.\n* **Future:** will be done.\n* **Modals:** can be done, must be done.",
      "tags": ["passive voice", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 216,
      "title": "Active and passive voice",
      "subtitle": "When to use passive",
      "category": "Passive Voice",
      "explanation": "We use passive when:\n1. We don't know who did the action.\n2. The action is more important than the doer.\n3. The doer is obvious (The thief was arrested [by police]).",
      "tags": ["passive voice", "style"]
    },
    {
      "id": 217,
      "title": "Modal verbs of deduction",
      "subtitle": "Must, might, could, can't",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "Guessing based on evidence (Present).\n\n* **Must:** 90-100% sure it's true (He has a Ferrari; he **must** be rich).\n* **Can't:** 90-100% sure it's impossible (He is eating; he **can't** be hungry).\n* **May/Might/Could:** 50% possibility (He **might** be at home).",
      "tags": ["modals", "deduction"]
    },
    {
      "id": 218,
      "title": "First conditional, future time clauses",
      "subtitle": "Unless, as soon as",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Variations of the First Conditional.\n\n* **Unless:** If not (I won't go **unless** you go).\n* **As soon as:** Immediately when.\n* **Provided that:** Only if.\n* Rule: Do not use 'will' in the 'if/when' clause.",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "future clauses"]
    },
    {
      "id": 219,
      "title": "Second conditional",
      "subtitle": "Unreal situations",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Imaginary present/future.\n\n* **If + Past Simple, ... would + Infinitive.**\n* Use 'If I were you' for advice.\n* Can use 'could' instead of 'would' for ability.",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "second conditional"]
    },
    {
      "id": 220,
      "title": "Third conditional",
      "subtitle": "Past unreal situations",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Regrets or imaginary past situations (impossible to change).\n\n* **Structure:** If + Past Perfect, ... would have + V3.\n* Example: If I **had studied**, I **would have passed** (But I didn't study, and I didn't pass).",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "third conditional"]
    },
    {
      "id": 221,
      "title": "Indirect speech",
      "subtitle": "Reported speech statements & questions",
      "category": "Reported Speech",
      "explanation": "Reporting what someone said.\n\n* **Backshift:** Present -> Past, Past -> Past Perfect, Will -> Would.\n* **Questions:** Word order changes to Statement order. (He asked where **I lived** - NOT where did I live).\n* **Commands:** Use 'to + infinitive' (He told me **to stop**).",
      "tags": ["reported speech", "indirect questions"]
    },
    {
      "id": 222,
      "title": "Gerund or infinitive",
      "subtitle": "Stop to do vs Stop doing",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Verbs where meaning changes.\n\n* **Stop doing:** Quit an action (I stopped smoking).\n* **Stop to do:** Pause to do something else (I stopped to buy milk).\n* **Remember doing:** Recall a memory.\n* **Remember to do:** Don't forget a task.",
      "tags": ["gerund", "infinitive"]
    },
    {
      "id": 223,
      "title": "Quantifiers: Much, many, a lot, little, few, some, any, no",
      "subtitle": "Review and advanced use",
      "category": "Quantifiers",
      "explanation": "Nuances in usage.\n\n* **None:** Pronoun (How much money? None).\n* **No:** Determiner (I have no money).\n* **Any:** Can mean 'it doesn't matter which' in positive sentences (Come any time).",
      "tags": ["quantifiers", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 224,
      "title": "All, both",
      "subtitle": "Grouping",
      "category": "Quantifiers",
      "explanation": "**All:** 3 or more items/people.\n**Both:** 2 items/people.\n\n* **Both of** my parents.\n* **All (of)** the students.\n* Position: They are **both** happy / They **both** like pizza.",
      "tags": ["quantifiers", "both", "all"]
    },
    {
      "id": 225,
      "title": "Both, either, neither",
      "subtitle": "Pairs",
      "category": "Quantifiers",
      "explanation": "Talking about two things.\n\n* **Both:** A and B (Positive).\n* **Either:** A or B (Choice).\n* **Neither:** Not A and Not B (Negative).",
      "tags": ["quantifiers", "either", "neither"]
    },
    {
      "id": 226,
      "title": "So, such, such a",
      "subtitle": "Intensifiers",
      "category": "Adjectives",
      "explanation": "Used to emphasize qualities.\n\n* **So + Adjective:** It was **so** cold.\n* **Such + Noun Phrase:** It was **such** cold weather.\n* **Such a + Singular Countable:** He is **such a** nice boy.\n* **So much/many:** Quantity.",
      "tags": ["intensifiers", "so vs such"]
    },
    {
      "id": 227,
      "title": "Defining and non-defining relative clauses",
      "subtitle": "Commas vs No commas",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "**Defining (No commas):** Essential info. 'The man who lives here is tall.'\n**Non-defining (Commas):** Extra info. 'My brother, who lives here, is tall.'\n* **Note:** Cannot use 'that' in non-defining clauses.",
      "tags": ["relative clauses", "punctuation"]
    },
    {
      "id": 228,
      "title": "Question tags",
      "subtitle": "Aren't you? Don't you?",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Short questions at the end of sentences to check info.\n\n* Positive sentence -> Negative tag (You are Tom, **aren't you**?).\n* Negative sentence -> Positive tag (You don't smoke, **do you**?).\n* Exceptions: I am -> **aren't I**? / Let's -> **shall we**?",
      "tags": ["question tags", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 229,
      "title": "Clauses of contrast, purpose and reason",
      "subtitle": "In spite of, so that, due to",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "**Contrast:** Although / Even though vs In spite of / Despite (+ Noun/-ing).\n**Purpose:** To / In order to vs So that (+ Subject + Verb).\n**Reason:** Because / Since / As vs Due to / Because of (+ Noun).",
      "tags": ["connectors", "linking words"]
    },
    {
      "id": 230,
      "title": "Verb + preposition",
      "subtitle": "Dependent prepositions",
      "category": "Prepositions",
      "explanation": "Verbs that always take a specific preposition.\n\n* Depend **on**\n* Believe **in**\n* Wait **for**\n* Succeed **in**\n* Apologize **for**\n* Belong **to**",
      "tags": ["prepositions", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 231,
      "title": "Adjective + preposition",
      "subtitle": "Dependent prepositions",
      "category": "Prepositions",
      "explanation": "Adjectives that always take a specific preposition.\n\n* Good/Bad **at**\n* Interested **in**\n* Afraid **of**\n* Married **to**\n* Famous **for**\n* Similar **to**",
      "tags": ["prepositions", "adjectives"]
    },
    {
      "id": 232,
      "title": "Had better ... it's time",
      "subtitle": "Strong advice and urgency",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "**Had better:** Strong advice/warning (You had better leave now).\n**It's time:**\n* **It's time to go** (Infinitive).\n* **It's time we went** (Past subjunctive meaning 'now').",
      "tags": ["modals", "phrases"]
    },
    {
      "id": 233,
      "title": "For, since, from",
      "subtitle": "Time prepositions",
      "category": "Prepositions",
      "explanation": "**For:** Duration.\n**Since:** Starting point up to now (with Perfect tenses).\n**From:** Starting point (can be used with other tenses).\n* I work **from** 9 to 5.",
      "tags": ["prepositions", "time"]
    },
    {
      "id": 234,
      "title": "Compound adjectives with numbers",
      "subtitle": "A two-day trip",
      "category": "Adjectives",
      "explanation": "When a number and a noun are used as an adjective before another noun, the first noun becomes singular and hyphenated.\n\n* A walk of 5 miles -> A **five-mile** walk.\n* A boy of 10 years -> A **ten-year-old** boy.",
      "tags": ["adjectives", "compound"]
    },
    {
      "id": 235,
      "title": "B1 Phrasal verbs",
      "subtitle": "Common phrasal verbs",
      "category": "Phrasal Verbs",
      "explanation": "Essential phrasal verbs for B1.\n\n* **Look forward to** (wait with pleasure).\n* **Run out of** (have no more).\n* **Get on with** (have a good relationship).\n* **Put up with** (tolerate).",
      "tags": ["phrasal verbs", "vocabulary"]
    },
    {
      "id": 236,
      "title": "Would rather & Would sooner",
      "subtitle": "Preferences",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Expressing preference.\n\n* **Same subject:** I would rather stay home (Base verb).\n* **Different subject:** I would rather **you stayed** home (Past Subjunctive).\n* Similar to 'prefer', but specific structure.",
      "tags": ["preferences", "would rather"]
    }
  ]
}

agora ajuste o curriculo do B1+ no modo estudo: {
  "database_info": {
    "level": "B1+",
    "level_description": "Upper-intermediate Grammar",
    "source_domain": "test-english.com",
    "total_lessons": 36,
    "last_updated": "2025-12-07"
  },
  "lessons": [
    {
      "id": 301,
      "title": "Present perfect simple or continuous",
      "subtitle": "Duration vs Result",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Advanced contrast between these two forms.\n\n* **Continuous:** Focus on the activity, duration, or explanation for a present state (My hands are dirty because I've been gardening).\n* **Simple:** Focus on the result or completion (I've planted three rose bushes).\n* **Note:** With 'live' and 'work', there is often little difference.",
      "tags": ["present perfect", "continuous", "simple"]
    },
    {
      "id": 302,
      "title": "Narrative tenses: All past tenses",
      "subtitle": "Past Simple, Continuous, Perfect, Perfect Continuous",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Using all past tenses together to tell a complex story.\n\n* **Past Simple:** Main events (He arrived).\n* **Past Continuous:** Background (The sun was shining).\n* **Past Perfect:** Previous events (He realized he had forgotten his keys).\n* **Past Perfect Continuous:** Duration before the past moment (He had been driving for hours when...)." ,
      "tags": ["narrative", "past tenses", "storytelling"]
    },
    {
      "id": 303,
      "title": "Future continuous and future perfect",
      "subtitle": "Will be doing vs Will have done",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "**Future Continuous (will be + -ing):** Action in progress at a specific future time (At 8 PM, I will be eating dinner).\n**Future Perfect (will have + V3):** Action finished *before* a specific future time (By 8 PM, I will have finished work).",
      "tags": ["future", "future perfect", "future continuous"]
    },
    {
      "id": 304,
      "title": "When I do vs When I have done",
      "subtitle": "Future time clauses",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "In future time clauses (after when, as soon as, unless), we use present tenses, not 'will'.\n\n* **Present Simple:** Sequence is not emphasized (When I get home, I'll call you).\n* **Present Perfect:** Emphasizes completion *before* the next action (We can't start until he **has arrived**).",
      "tags": ["future", "time clauses", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 305,
      "title": "Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to, needn't have",
      "subtitle": "Absence of obligation",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "**Present:** 'You needn't wait' is similar to 'You don't need to wait'.\n**Past:**\n* **Didn't need to:** We didn't do it because it wasn't necessary.\n* **Needn't have done:** We *did* it, but later realized it wasn't necessary (A waste of time).",
      "tags": ["modals", "obligation", "need"]
    },
    {
      "id": 306,
      "title": "Past modal verbs of deduction",
      "subtitle": "Must have, can't have, might have",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "Deducing what happened in the past.\n\n* **Must have + V3:** 99% sure it happened (He's late; he must have missed the bus).\n* **Can't have + V3:** 99% sure it didn't happen (He can't have eaten it; he hates fish).\n* **Might/Could have + V3:** Possibility (He might have forgotten).",
      "tags": ["modals", "deduction", "past"]
    },
    {
      "id": 307,
      "title": "Likely, unlikely, bound, definitely, probably",
      "subtitle": "Probability expressions",
      "category": "Adjectives and Adverbs",
      "explanation": "Alternatives to modals for expressing probability.\n\n* **Be bound to:** Certainty (He is bound to win).\n* **Be likely to:** Probability (It is likely to rain).\n* **Definitely/Probably:** Adverbs position (He will **definitely** go / He **definitely** won't go).",
      "tags": ["probability", "vocabulary"]
    },
    {
      "id": 308,
      "title": "Used to, be used to, get used to",
      "subtitle": "Habits vs Familiarity",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Essential B1+ distinction.\n* **Used to + Verb:** Past habit (I used to smoke).\n* **Be used to + -ing:** Current familiarity (I am used to getting up early).\n* **Get used to + -ing:** Process of adaptation (I am getting used to the noise).",
      "tags": ["used to", "habits", "adaptation"]
    },
    {
      "id": 309,
      "title": "Would and used to",
      "subtitle": "Past habits and repeated actions",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Both express past habits, but 'would' has limitations.\n\n* **Used to:** Works for actions AND states (I used to live here).\n* **Would:** Works ONLY for repeated actions, not states (Every Sunday we would visit grandma). *Incorrect: I would have a bike.*",
      "tags": ["past habits", "would", "used to"]
    },
    {
      "id": 310,
      "title": "Verbs of the senses",
      "subtitle": "Look, sound, feel, taste, smell",
      "category": "Verbs",
      "explanation": "Structures following sense verbs.\n\n* **+ Adjective:** You look **tired**.\n* **+ Like + Noun:** It sounds **like a bird**.\n* **+ As if/As though + Clause:** It smells **as if** something is burning.",
      "tags": ["senses", "verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 311,
      "title": "Zero and first conditional and future time clauses",
      "subtitle": "Real situations",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Review and expansion.\n* **Zero:** Facts (If you heat ice, it melts).\n* **First:** Real future (If it rains, I'll stay home).\n* **Time Clauses:** Never use 'will' after *when, as soon as, until, before, after*.",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "zero conditional", "first conditional"]
    },
    {
      "id": 312,
      "title": "Second and third conditionals",
      "subtitle": "Unreal conditionals",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Distinguishing hypothetical present vs past.\n\n* **Second (Present/Future):** If I **had** time, I **would go**.\n* **Third (Past Regret):** If I **had had** time, I **would have gone** (But I didn't have time).",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "second conditional", "third conditional"]
    },
    {
      "id": 313,
      "title": "Wishes and regrets: I wish / if only",
      "subtitle": "Desiring change",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "**I wish / If only...**\n* **+ Past Simple:** Change present state (I wish I was rich).\n* **+ Past Perfect:** Regret about past (I wish I hadn't eaten that).\n* **+ Would:** Annoyance/Desire for behavior change (I wish you would stop talking).",
      "tags": ["wishes", "regrets", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 314,
      "title": "The passive voice: All tenses",
      "subtitle": "Comprehensive review",
      "category": "Passive Voice",
      "explanation": "Applying passive to complex tenses.\n\n* **Present Perfect Passive:** The road **has been closed**.\n* **Past Continuous Passive:** The room **was being cleaned**.\n* **Modals:** It **should be done**.",
      "tags": ["passive voice", "tenses"]
    },
    {
      "id": 315,
      "title": "The passive with reporting verbs",
      "subtitle": "It is said that...",
      "category": "Passive Voice",
      "explanation": "Formal way to report news or rumors.\n\n* **Structure 1:** It is said/thought/believed **that** he is rich.\n* **Structure 2 (Personal):** He is said/thought/believed **to be** rich.",
      "tags": ["passive voice", "reporting verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 316,
      "title": "Have something done",
      "subtitle": "Causative form",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "When we arrange for someone else to do a service for us.\n\n* **Structure:** Have + Object + Past Participle.\n* I **had my hair cut** (I didn't cut it myself).\n* We are **having the house painted**.",
      "tags": ["causative", "have something done"]
    },
    {
      "id": 317,
      "title": "Gerund or infinitive: Verb patterns",
      "subtitle": "Complex patterns",
      "category": "Verbs",
      "explanation": "Focus on verbs that change meaning (try, stop, regret, remember, forget).\n\n* **Try doing:** Experiment.\n* **Try to do:** Attempt difficulty.\n* **Regret doing:** Sorry about past.\n* **Regret to say:** Sorry to announce bad news.",
      "tags": ["gerund", "infinitive", "verb patterns"]
    },
    {
      "id": 318,
      "title": "Reporting verbs",
      "subtitle": "Admit, refuse, deny, suggest",
      "category": "Reported Speech",
      "explanation": "Using specific verbs instead of just 'said'.\n\n* **Verb + -ing:** He **admitted stealing** the money.\n* **Verb + to + infinitive:** He **refused to go**.\n* **Verb + that:** He **explained that**...",

      "title": "Whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever, however",

agora ajuste o curriculo do B2 no modo estudo: {
  "database_info": {
    "level": "B2",
    "level_description": "Pre-advanced Grammar",
    "source_domain": "test-english.com",
    "total_lessons": 35,
    "last_updated": "2025-12-07"
  },
  "lessons": [
    {
      "id": 401,
      "title": "Have: Auxiliary or main verb",
      "subtitle": "Dynamic vs Stative uses",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Understanding 'have' in different roles.\n\n* **Auxiliary:** Helping verb for Perfect tenses (I have eaten). Cannot use 'do/did' in questions/negatives here.\n* **Main Verb (Possession):** Stative (I have a car). No continuous form.\n* **Main Verb (Action):** Dynamic (I am having lunch). Can be continuous. Requires 'do/did' for questions/negatives.",
      "tags": ["have", "auxiliary verbs", "stative verbs"]
    },
    {
      "id": 402,
      "title": "Clauses of contrast, purpose, reason and result",
      "subtitle": "Complex linkers",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Advanced connectors.\n\n* **Contrast:** Even though, despite the fact that, while, whereas.\n* **Purpose:** So as to, in order to, for fear that, in case.\n* **Reason:** Due to the fact that, owing to, since, as.\n* **Result:** Consequently, as a result, thus, therefore.",
      "tags": ["connectors", "linking words", "clauses"]
    },
    {
      "id": 403,
      "title": "Generic or common-gender pronouns",
      "subtitle": "They/Them for singular",
      "category": "Pronouns",
      "explanation": "Using pronouns when gender is unknown or irrelevant.\n\n* **They/Them/Their:** Used as a singular pronoun for a person of unspecified gender.\n* Example: 'If **a student** calls, tell **them** I am busy.'\n* Avoids 'he or she' or 'him or her'.",
      "tags": ["pronouns", "gender", "generic"]
    },
    {
      "id": 404,
      "title": "Reflexive and reciprocal pronouns",
      "subtitle": "Themselves vs Each other",
      "category": "Pronouns",
      "explanation": "Distinction between self-action and mutual action.\n\n* **Reflexive (Themselves):** They looked at **themselves** in the mirror (A sees A, B sees B).\n* **Reciprocal (Each other / One another):** They looked at **each other** (A sees B, B sees A).",
      "tags": ["reflexive", "reciprocal", "pronouns"]
    },
    {
      "id": 405,
      "title": "'There' and 'it': Preparatory subjects",
      "subtitle": "Placeholder subjects",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Using dummy subjects to shift focus.\n\n* **There:** Existence or presence (There appears to be a mistake).\n* **It:** Anticipatory subject for infinitives/clauses (It is important **to study**).\n* **It + Passive:** It is said that...",
      "tags": ["preparatory subject", "there vs it"]
    },
    {
      "id": 406,
      "title": "Narrative tenses, used to, would",
      "subtitle": "Advanced storytelling",
      "category": "Verbs and Tenses",
      "explanation": "Complex past narration combining habits and specific events.\n\n* **Past Perfect Continuous:** Background duration.\n* **Would:** Repeated past actions (nostalgic tone).\n* **Used to:** Past states and habits.\n* **Past Simple:** Sequential actions advancing the plot.",
      "tags": ["narrative", "storytelling", "past"]
    },
    {
      "id": 407,
      "title": "Get: Different meanings",
      "subtitle": "Causative, passive, movement",
      "category": "Verbs",
      "explanation": "Mastering the versatility of 'get'.\n\n* **Obtain/Receive:** Get a job.\n* **Become:** Get angry.\n* **Arrive:** Get to work.\n* **Passive (Informal):** Get fired, get paid.\n* **Causative:** Get him to do it (Persuade).",
      "tags": ["get", "causative", "vocabulary"]
    },
    {
      "id": 408,
      "title": "Discourse markers: Linking words",
      "subtitle": "Structuring arguments",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Words to organize speech and writing.\n\n* **Ordering:** Firstly, furthermore, finally.\n* **Generalizing:** On the whole, broadly speaking.\n* **Clarifying:** In other words, that is to say.\n* **Concluding:** All in all, to sum up.",
      "tags": ["discourse markers", "writing"]
    },
    {
      "id": 409,
      "title": "Speculation and deduction: Modal verbs and expressions",
      "subtitle": "Bound to, likely to, must have",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "Degrees of certainty.\n\n* **Almost certain:** Must, can't, bound to.\n* **Probable:** Likely to, should, ought to.\n* **Possible:** May, might, could.\n* Includes continuous forms: 'He must **be sleeping**'.",
      "tags": ["deduction", "speculation", "modals"]
    },
    {
      "id": 410,
      "title": "Inversion with negative adverbials",
      "subtitle": "Adding emphasis",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Formal structure: Negative Adverb + Auxiliary + Subject.\n\n* **Never** have I seen such a thing.\n* **Not only** did he arrive late, **but** he also forgot his bag.\n* **Under no circumstances** should you open this door.\n* **Hardly** had I arrived **when** the phone rang.",
      "tags": ["inversion", "emphasis", "formal"]
    },
    {
      "id": 411,
      "title": "Distancing: Expressions and passive of reporting verbs",
      "subtitle": "It seems, appeared to be",
      "category": "Passive Voice",
      "explanation": "Techniques to sound objective or unsure.\n\n* **Seem/Appear:** It seems that... / He appears to be...\n* **Passive Reporting:** It is believed that... / She is rumoured to be...\n* **Apparently / Supposedly:** Adverbs of distancing.",
      "tags": ["distancing", "reporting", "passive"]
    },
    {
      "id": 412,
      "title": "Wish, rather, if only, it's time",
      "subtitle": "Unreal past tenses",
      "category": "Structure",
      "explanation": "Using past tenses for present/future hypothetical meaning.\n\n* **It's time:** It's time we **went** (Present meaning).\n* **I'd rather:** I'd rather you **didn't** smoke (Present/Future preference).\n* **If only:** Stronger version of 'I wish'.",
      "tags": ["subjunctive", "unreal past", "wishes"]
    },
    {
      "id": 413,
      "title": "Verb + object + infinitive/gerund",
      "subtitle": "Complex verb patterns",
      "category": "Verbs",
      "explanation": "Verbs taking an object before the second verb.\n\n* **Verb + Object + to...:** I want **you to help** me. (Advise, ask, expect, forbid).\n* **Verb + Object + -ing:** I saw **him stealing** the car. (Hear, smell, feel - sense perception of part of action).",
      "tags": ["verb patterns", "object", "infinitive"]
    },
    {
      "id": 414,
      "title": "Unless, even if, provided, as long as, etc.",
      "subtitle": "Conditionals without 'if'",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Alternatives to 'if'.\n\n* **Unless:** If not (I won't go unless you go).\n* **Provided (that) / As long as:** Condition is strictly necessary (You can drive as long as you have a license).\n* **Even if:** The result doesn't change (I'll go even if it rains).\n* **Suppose/Supposing:** Imaginary condition.",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "conjunctions"]
    },
    {
      "id": 415,
      "title": "All conditionals: Mixed, alternatives, inversion",
      "subtitle": "Advanced conditional structures",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Mastery of conditional forms.\n\n* **Inversion (First):** **Should** you need help... (= If you should need).\n* **Inversion (Second):** **Were** I you... (= If I were you).\n* **Inversion (Third):** **Had** I known... (= If I had known).",
      "tags": ["conditionals", "inversion", "mixed"]
    },
    {
      "id": 416,
      "title": "Mixed conditionals",
      "subtitle": "If I were you, I wouldn't have done it",
      "category": "Conditionals",
      "explanation": "Combining 2nd and 3rd types.\n\n* **Past Action -> Present Result:** If I **hadn't spent** all my money (Past), I **would be** rich now (Present).\n* **Present State -> Past Result:** If I **were** smarter (General state), I **wouldn't have failed** the exam (Past event).",
      "tags": ["mixed conditionals", "grammar"]
    },
    {
      "id": 417,
      "title": "Modal verbs: Permission, obligation, prohibition, necessity",
      "subtitle": "Advanced nuances",
      "category": "Modals",
      "explanation": "Subtle differences.\n\n* **Must vs Have to:** Internal vs External obligation.\n* **Needn't vs Don't have to:** Lack of necessity.\n* **Be supposed to:** Expectation or rule (often unfulfilled).\n* **Be allowed to / Can:** Permission.",
      "tags": ["modals", "obligation"]
    },
    {
      "id": 418,
      "title": "Verbs of the senses",
